definition: A placement test is an academic test students take before being assigned to a school placement, with the results used as a score related to where they are placed. In this study, it was given during a secondary school transition and served as a measure of students’ academic performance.

reasons: The packet supports that placement test scores were collected during a secondary school transition, but it does not state that the results were used to determine where students were placed.
The definition adds a specific function for the test’s results as a placement score; that use is not established in the source text.

The packet does not explicitly state that placement test results are used “as a score related to where they are placed” or that the test directly determines school placement assignment; it only mentions that students later “learn their school placement” (T3) and that they have “placement test scores (T1+).”

The definition claims the test is “before being assigned to a school placement” and that “results [are] used” for placement; while T1 precedes T3, the packet does not explicitly describe the test’s role in assignment.

The packet supports that the placement test occurs during a secondary school transition and that placement test scores are used alongside prior grades, but the definition’s placement-assignment mechanism is not clearly supported.
